steps.title: Reversible reaction
steps.body: A reaction in which the products can react together to re-form the original reactants. Shown by the symbol ⇌ instead of →.

steps.title: Dynamic equilibrium
steps.body: The state reached in a closed system where the forward and backward reactions occur at the same rate, so the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant.

steps.title: Le Chatelier's principle
steps.body: If a change is made to the conditions of a system at equilibrium, the position of equilibrium shifts to oppose the change.

steps.title: Closed system
steps.body: A system where no substances can enter or leave. Dynamic equilibrium can only be reached in a closed system.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: When a reversible reaction takes place in a closed system , eventually the forward and backward reactions happen at the same rate . This is called dynamic equilibrium. Features of dynamic equilibrium: The forward and backward reactions are still happening (dynamic) Their rates are equal, so there is no overall change (equilibrium) Concentrations of reactants and products stay constant — but are not necessarily equal It can only be reached in a closed system Worked Example 2: Understanding equilibrium In the equilibrium: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), explain what is happening at equilibrium. Nitrogen and hydrogen are still reacting to form ammonia (forward reaction). Ammonia is still decomposing back into nitrogen and hydrogen (backward reaction). Both reactions happen at the same rate. The concentrations of N₂, H₂ and NH₃ remain constant.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When applying Le Chatelier's principle, always state the direction of shift first, then the effect on yield For temperature questions, first identify which direction is endothermic and which is exothermic For pressure questions, count the moles of GAS on each side — only gas moles matter A catalyst does NOT change the position of equilibrium — it only helps equilibrium be reached faster In Haber process questions, always explain the compromise between yield and rate When asked about dynamic equilibrium, mention: closed system, forward = backward rate, concentrations constant Remember: "shift to the right" means more products; "shift to the left" means more reactants
